fact: Space in Africa reports Zambia is among the top three African countries by Starlink subscribers (with Nigeria and Zimbabwe, about 64% of roughly 300,000 African customers) as of June 2026; the figure is an analyst's, not the regulator's.

Paratus Zambia is an authorised Starlink reseller and network services provider in Zambia, under a reseller agreement signed September 2023, and Starlink launched business services in Zambia in October 2023.

Space in Africa estimates roughly 300,000 African Starlink subscribers as of June 2026, with Nigeria, Zimbabwe and Zambia holding about 64% of them between them, implying Starlink is on sale in Zambia; no Zambia-only count is given.
Starlink's status table for African countries, dated 17 July 2026, lists Zambia as Available.
Starlink lists Zambia among 26 countries 'Active Now' as of the article; Zambia prices are given in ZMW and measured speeds of 181 Mbps down, 24 Mbps up.

Starlink's demand outstripped allocated capacity in 2025-2026, forcing suspended new residential sign-ups in some markets; the article says similar freezes have hit Zambia, so the service was on sale there; it also says Paratus's EduLink reseller programme extended Starlink-powered connectivity to schools in Zambia.
Zambia is listed among markets that approved Starlink quickly, without local-ownership requirements or with them set aside; no date or licence detail given, so the article's published date is used.
Starlink is stated to be already operational in Zambia, among other African countries, extending connectivity to rural areas; no date given, so the article's published date is used.

The article says Zambia, like Nigeria, allowed satellite operator entry within a negotiated framework with regulatory scrutiny of pricing; it names no provider for Zambia and gives no date, so the article date is used.
